Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Welcome from the Head Teacher
A very warm welcome to St Margaret’s Church of England (VA) Primary School, Angmering.
At the heart of our school is our vision: Created to Shine! We strive to be a shining light of love, aspiration and excellence, helping every child grow into the person God intended them to be.
"You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden." Matthew 5:14
Through our values of love and aspiration, we aim to shine brightly—making a difference in our school, community and the wider world.
We warmly invite you to visit us and discover what makes St Margaret’s so special. Please also enjoy exploring our website to learn more about our wonderful school.
Mr George Lumley Headteacher
Considering a school place for September 2027? Join us for our Open Evening, an Autumn Term Tour or a Stay and Play Session to discover how every child is encouraged to grow, thrive and shine at St Margaret's.
Two groups of recent recipients of our Shining Star award! We're all so proud of each and every one of you!
Keeping children safe matters all year round. If you're worried about a child during the summer holidays, please reach out to the West Sussex Integrated Front Door. Someone is always there to help.
The end of another fantastic year at St Margaret's! We all hope you have a restful summer making wonderful memories with your lovely children. A big thank you for all the incredibly generous cards, messages and gifts to all our staff - it's greatly appreciated by everyone. See you in September for another brilliant year!

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
Community & Partnerships
Community & Partnerships
Matthew 5 calls us to be 'City on a hill' - we want to let our light as a school shine brightly and beyond the walls of the school. We want to extend our work in the local community and serve others. We believe this is important in not only demonstrating God's love to others, but in helping children learn more about the world around them and their responsibilities within it.
We have recently established a partnership with Ayton House nursing home and are working together on several projects with the residents in a range of enrichment activities. This term, we have seen the start of a new book club, where residents from Ayton House come to school for the afternoon and spend time with the children sharing a book together.
Currently, we have a Foodbank Collection point in the school reception area and are able to refer families who may need support to Littlehampton Foodbank as well as the support offered by the local charity, Family Support Work CDA - based out of St Margaret's Church.
We also donate pre-loved uniform to local mission partners who send school uniform to a school in Madagascar.
We are looking forward to working alongside the Library in Angmering to help develop a new garden space.
We are on the look out for local (and further afield!) opportunities to work together in partnership - please be in touch if you have links, or ideas in which would help us grow this work.

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Governors
Our Governing Board is made up of enthusiastic and hardworking volunteers with an interest, passion and commitment to the education of children. Our Board consists of parents, school staff and volunteers appointed by the local authority and Chichester Church of England Diocese.
Governors play an important part in overseeing the running of the school in the interests of the community it serves. We work in partnership with the school, making decisions about, for example, educational standards and targets, policies, staffing and finance, whilst ensuring our school’s Christian vision ‘Created to Shine’, and our values of Love and Aspire, are at the very heart of all we do.
Our role is to govern rather than to manage, leaving the Headteacher and his team responsible for the day to day running of the school.
Our core functions are to:
Individual governors have no power or responsibility. It is only the full governing body which has legal duties and powers and all governors share in that corporate responsibility. If you are interested in finding out more about being a governor, please contact us via the school. We would be very happy to discuss the role further, how we carry out our responsibilities, and any possible vacancies on the board.

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
SEND
At St Margaret's CE Primary School, our Christian vision that every child is 'Created to Shine' underpins every aspect of school life. We believe every child is uniquely created by God, valued equally and deserving of an education that enables them to flourish academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually.
Our core values of Love and Aspire shape our commitment to inclusive education. We strive to create a nurturing, ambitious and welcoming community where every pupil experiences belonging, feels safe, is respected and is supported to achieve their full potential.
Our SEND provision is built around strong relationships with families. We know every child's journey is different, and we work in partnership with parents to understand each child's strengths, needs and aspirations.
Our SENCo (Special Educational Needs coordinator) is Terri Challis she can be contacted on inclusion@stmargaretsprimary.org.uk
Targeted pastoral care enables pupils to live well together and flourish. Leaders ensure that pupils who have special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) receive effective support. A special support centre supports pupils with social communication needs. This provision enables pupils to access mainstream learning and experience success. Dedicated staff work with love and aspiration to help these pupils to ‘shine’. This inclusive approach reflects the school’s commitment to meeting the needs of every pupil. Staff celebrate pupils’ progress and personal achievements across the school community
SIAMS inspection report, may 2026
We understand that navigating SEND can sometimes feel overwhelming and that every family's journey is different. These frequently asked questions explain how we support children and work in partnership with families. If you cannot find the information you need, please contact us, we are always happy to help.
What is SEND?
Some children need additional support to help them learn and make progress in school.
A child may have Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND) if they have a learning difficulty or disability that means they require educational provision that is additional to or different from that normally available for children of the same age.
Children's needs can change over time, and support is reviewed regularly to ensure it remains appropriate.
How do you identify if a child may have SEND?
We get to know every child as an individual and carefully monitor their learning, wellbeing and progress.
Sometimes a parent may raise a concern, and sometimes a teacher may notice that a child is finding certain areas more challenging than expected. When this happens, we will work together to build a fuller picture of your child's strengths and needs.
classroom observations
discussions with parents and the child
assessment information
information from previous schools or settings
advice from other professionals where appropriate
Some children need additional support for a short period of time, while others may benefit from long term SEND Support.
What is SEND Support?
SEND Support is the additional help provided when a child needs more than high quality classroom teaching alone.
Support is planned using the graduated approach:
Assess, Plan, Do, Review
This ensures support is carefully planned, monitored and adapted as your child develops.
Does having a diagnosis automatically mean my child will receive SEND Support?
No. A diagnosis does not automatically mean a pupil requires SEND Support. Equally, pupils may receive SEND Support without a formal medical diagnosis where evidence shows that additional educational provision is required.
Some children with a diagnosis make excellent progress through high quality classroom teaching and reasonable adjustments alone.
Equally, some children without a formal diagnosis require SEND Support because they need educational provision that is additional to or different from that ordinarily available.
How will my child be supported?
Every child receives high quality inclusive teaching from their class teacher.
Where appropriate, teachers adapt teaching through strategies such as:
Pre teaching vocabulary
additional processing time
assistive technology
If further support is needed, this is planned through the graduated approach of Assess, Plan, Do and Review.
Who will support my child?
Your child's class teacher is responsible for their learning and progress. Support may also be provided by:
Learning Support Assistants
Pastoral support in school
staff from The Tomlin Centre (where appropriate)
external specialists working alongside school staff
All support is planned to complement inclusive classroom teaching rather than replace it.
How will I know how my child is getting on?
We work in partnership with parents throughout the year. You can expect:
regular communication with your child's teacher
meetings with the SENCo when appropriate
Annual Reviews for pupils with an EHCP
We have an open door policy and encourage parents to contact us whenever they have questions or concerns.
What if I think my child has SEND?
If you have concerns about your child's learning or development, please speak to your child's class teacher in the first instance. They know your child best and can discuss your concerns, explain what support is already in place and agree any next steps. If appropriate, the SENCo may also become involved.
My child is joining St Margaret's. How will you support their transition?
We work closely with nurseries, previous schools and families to ensure a smooth transition.
Where appropriate, we will:
meet with you before your child starts with us
visit your child's previous setting
share information with professionals
arrange additional visits to school
prepare staff so support is in place from the first day
We aim to help every child feel safe, confident and ready to learn.
What happens if my child has an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP)?
Children with an EHCP receive support that reflects the provision outlined in their Education, Health and Care Plan. The SENCo works closely with families, staff and external professionals to ensure provision is delivered effectively.
An Annual Review is held each year to review progress and consider whether any changes are needed.
Who can I contact to discuss concerns about my child’s needs?
The first point of contact will always be your child’s class teacher. The SENCo at St Margaret’s is Terri Challis and can be available for further support at inclusion@stmargaretsprimary.org.uk
Where can I go for more information on SEND?
You can access the West Sussex Local Offer via the West Sussex County Council website. The Local Offer is a clear, central place that explains what help is available for children and young people (0 - 25) with SEND, and how families can access it.
You can also contact the SEND Information, Advice and Support Service (SENDIAS). SENDIAS is a free, confidential and independent service in West Sussex that supports parents, carers, and young people to understand and navigate the SEND system. Their role is to make sure families feel informed, supported, and confident when making decisions about their child’s education and wellbeing. You can contact SENDIAS on 0330 222 8555 or visit their website to complete a contact form www.westsussexsendias.org
If you would like to learn more about our approach to SEND, please click the tabs below to access our policies, information report and other useful documents.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
Curriculum
St Margaret’s CE Primary School
Our Curriculum Intent
At St Margaret’s CE Primary School we want our curriculum to reflect our mission – our reason for being here. At its heart we seek a curriculum that serves the needs of the child both educationally and spiritually, a curriculum that provides deep foundations for learning and which prepares children socially and emotionally for a complex but exciting world.
We want a curriculum that is both knowledge rich, experience driven and leads to learning that equips and prepares. Children should be encouraged to think deeply and critically, follow their own interests and develop expertise in subject disciplines.
Our curriculum encourages excellence, values effort and celebrates achievement. Together, our learning is creative, enriching and relevant to today and tomorrow.
The outworking of our curriculum is simple. We want our children to be the best they can be; to reach their potential; to be true to themselves, growing in wisdom and able to make good choices now and throughout their lives. Our children respect themselves and others, are self- confident, empathetic and have inner peace and optimism for the future.
Driving our curriculum is our vision, Created to Shine!
Built upon our vision of ‘Created to shine’, our curriculum projects in Create, Discover and Explore are carefully designed and sequenced to empower each child to shine in their own unique way. Our children move beyond acquiring ‘head knowledge’ and develop ‘heart knowledge’- internalised values that guide their choices and actions. Our curriculum acts as a vehicle for teaching truths that make a positive difference in the individual lives of our children, families, community and beyond. By the time our children reach the end of their journey at St Margaret’s, our children will be distinctively different. Not only will they be equipped with strong academic foundations but they will have internalised values and character that allow them to shine in all aspects of life.
As a school, we have carefully considered what it means for our children to truly shine. Shining encompasses qualities such as loving others, making good choices, seeking truth and wonder and being a courageous, loving leader. These attributes are mapped progressively across each year group, ensuring that pupils develop the knowledge, skills and values to embody them as they move through the school and beyond.
Reflecting the vision, leaders consider how pupils can shine through their learning experiences. This understanding shapes the curriculum effectively. Inspiring projects encourage pupils to create, discover and explore. For example, pupils consider the question, ‘If the world could speak, what would it say?’ As a result, pupils understand environmental responsibility and care for the world.
SIAMS inspection report, may 2026
Spiritual Development
Therefore, projects and learning experiences are deliberately designed with ‘shining’ as the end goal. These qualities become the substantive concepts that run through the projects like a golden thread, giving purpose, authenticity and coherence to our children’s learning and most importantly refocusing it back to our school vision of being ‘Created to shine’. Each year group has clearly defined end goals that build progressively as part of the bigger picture and their Spiritual Development.
Our curriculum draws on the National Curriculum for propositional knowledge but adds to this bank where appropriate for our children. We are mapping our procedural knowledge to develop children’s skills from Reception to Year 6.
Reading is at the heart of the curriculum so that children can unlock the door to learning at an early age.
We teach subjects through projects and discreetly where appropriate and continuously assess children’s learning and progress in order to tailor learning opportunities to meet their needs.

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
Equality & Diversity
Equality & Diversity
At our school, we believe every child is Created to Shine. We celebrate each child’s individuality and are committed to building a community where everyone feels loved, respected, and inspired to reach their full potential. Our core values of Love and Aspire guide us in creating an environment where diversity is embraced, inclusion is lived out daily, and equality is at the heart of everything we do.
Through our curriculum, assemblies, and school life, we encourage children to learn from one another, to appreciate differences, and to show kindness and empathy. By removing barriers and fostering aspiration, we support every child to flourish—academically, socially, and emotionally.
Our vision is for all pupils to leave our school with a deep sense of belonging, the confidence to be themselves, and the understanding that they have been Created to Shine in their own unique way.

Our History
Our History
Originally founded in 1680, William Older's Charity School, moved to our current site at the top of Arundel Road and became St Margaret's Church of England Primary School in 1965.
Still supported by the William Older Trust today, we are proud of our history and it is a privilege to be part of such a wonderful village and community here in Angmering.
Local Historian, Neil Rogers-Davis, has compiled a fascinating overview of the history of St Margaret's School which can be viewed on the Angmering Village website here:

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
The Worshipping Life of our School
The Worshipping Life of our School
At the heart of our Church of England school is our vision to be a shining light of love, aspiration and excellence that nurtures and enables all children to grow into the person God intended them to be.
Collective Worship at St Margaret's School As a Voluntary Aided Church of England school, daily collective worship is at the heart of our school life. It is a time when our whole community comes together to pause, reflect, and explore the Christian faith. Worship is inclusive, invitational, and inspiring – rooted in the teachings of Jesus and the values of the Church of England, while also offering space for personal reflection, whatever a child’s own beliefs.
Through stories, prayer, music, and reflection, children are encouraged to think about their place in the world, to develop spiritually and morally, and to live out our school’s Christian values in everyday life. Worship is central to nurturing our caring, respectful and inclusive community.
Monday - Whole School Collective Worship - a time to come together as a school, introduce a theme for the week, sing, and pray for the week ahead. Tuesday - Praise & Worship - a time of sung worship and reflection Wednesday - Key Stage Collective Worship - led by St Margaret's Church Thursday - Class or Year Group Collective Worship - we use this time to explore and reflect upon a current affairs issue using the resource Picture News for Church of England Schools. Friday - Whole School Collective Worship - a celebration and time of thanksgiving.
Attached at the bottom of this page is a document with the songs we have been singing in Collective Worship this year.
Collective worship brings the vision and values to life in inspiring and inclusive ways. School leaders and clergy work in partnership to plan carefully sequenced themes. These guide reflection and support spiritual understanding, in the context of collective worship. Themes are explored through Bible messages, supporting moral and social decision-making. A strong sense of community is developed through daily worship, involving singing, reflection and prayer.
SIAMS Inspection report, may 2026
Reflection and Prayer
Each class has a 'Reflection Area' to support opportunities to pause, reflect and pray - we have a whole school theme for the half term which classes will use.
We have times of daily prayer in classes - we have started to create a school prayer book to guide us during these times with contributions from the Church, staff and children.
The Church run a monthly Prayer Group who meet the first Friday of each month (term-time) at 9am in St Margaret's church vestry hall. (Situated at the upper end of car park through the iron gate). All are welcome to join.
We have a weekly prayer meeting for staff too 'Prayer and Pastries' on alternate Tuesday mornings, and 'Pause & Pray' on alternate Friday lunch times to pray for each other and to pray for the school.
Please follow this link to find out more about our Faith and Wonder curriculum - Faith and Wonder
We are very proud of our close relationship with our local St Margaret's church. Read more about our partnership here: St Margaret's Church
Our Christian Union ( Lighthouse Club) runs each week, led by the Youth and Children's Worker from St Margaret's Church.

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
Young Carers
Young Carers
We are committed to identifying and supporting Young Carers within our school community.
In July 2026, we were presented with the Young Carers in Schools award. Young carers are children under 18 who are responsible for the care of a family member with who, due to illness, disability, mental health condition or addiction, can’t cope without their support.
The award is part of the Young Carers in School programme run by charities The Children’s Society and Carers Trust. The programme provides primary and secondary schools across England with step-by-step guidance for teachers, leaders and non-teaching staff to gain the practical tools they need to help young carers.
We recognise that caring responsibilities can have a significant impact on a child’s wellbeing, attendance, and learning.
Our approach includes:
Ensuring staff are trained to recognise the signs that a child may be a Young Carer.
Providing pastoral support, adjustments, and additional help where needed.
Working in partnership with local Young Carers services to ensure families receive appropriate guidance and specialist support.
Creating a safe, understanding environment where Young Carers feel listened to and supported.
Vicky Morgan, Carers Trust’s Head of Young Carers at Young Adult Carers, said:
We’re delighted to present the Young Carers in Schools award to St Margaret's School. Figures show there are two young carers in every classroom but balancing learning with looking after family members can be tough without help. By identifying young carers and putting support in place, schools and teachers can make a huge difference to their wellbeing and education. That’s why the brilliant work done by staff at St Margaret's is so vital and why this award is so richly deserved.
If you would like more information about Young Carers, please speak with Mrs Darby.
West Sussex County Council also have lots of information to support Young Carers - please see their website through this link: https://www.westsussex.gov.uk/education-children-and-families/young-carers/#young-carers-family-service-eligibility-criteria

Welcome to St Margaret's CE Primary School
Our School
Behaviour
Behaviour
At St Margaret's School, we believe that every child is Created to Shine. We want our pupils to grow in confidence, kindness, and self-belief, supported by clear expectations and a nurturing environment. Our approach to behaviour is rooted in our core values of Love and Aspire: showing love through respect, kindness, care, and consideration for others, and aspiring to be the best version of ourselves each day.
Pupils demonstrate kindness, respect and positive behaviour in their relationships with others.
SIAMS Inspection report, may 2026
We have just developed a new behaviour policy that reflects these principles and provides a consistent, fair, and positive framework for all. This policy balances a restorative approach — helping children to learn from mistakes, repair relationships, and make better choices — with high expectations for conduct, effort, and respect.
We focus on recognising and celebrating positive behaviour, encouraging responsibility, and supporting pupils in developing the skills they need to manage their emotions and actions. At the same time, we are clear that boundaries are important. By combining compassion with high standards, we ensure that every child understands the importance of consideration for others and the impact of their choices.
Our aim is for every child to feel safe, valued, and empowered to thrive. By building a culture of love, aspiration, and respect, we help our pupils not only to succeed academically but also to grow into thoughtful, considerate individuals who shine in all aspects of life.
